page: Amazon Web Services m8gd.xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor and custom ARMv9 architecture. The instance provisions 4 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading, running AWS Neoverse-V2 CPUs clocked at 2.8 GHz. Memory capacity totals 16.0 GB, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The processor features 64 KB of L1 data cache per core, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 36 MB L3 cache. There are no discrete GPUs included, but the instance comes equipped with 237 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark measurements indicate balanced overall throughput with specific strengths and trade-offs. Synthetic compute evaluations place single-core and multi-core performance within average tiers across stress-ng (1707.38 single-core, 6816.76 multi-core) and Geekbench suites (1858.0 single-core, 5852.0 multi-core). Memory subsystem tests reveal solid bandwidth capabilities, registering 96.47 GB/sec for uncached read-only blocks and 44.54 GB/sec for large block writes. Compression performance is notable in single-threaded bzip3 decompression, which tests in the top 25 percent at 14.26 GB/sec. Conversely, PassMark cryptographic metrics register in lower tiers, and LLM text generation throughput drops significantly when processing larger models.

With its integrated NVMe storage volume and dedicated ARM core allocation, the m8gd.xlarge provides cost-efficient operational density for input-output demanding services that do not require x86 extensions. The instance is well matched for mid-sized relational and NoSQL databases, Redis caching layers, web application hosting, build systems, and general microservices pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services m8gd.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine driven by the ARMv9 AWS Neoverse-V2 processor on the Nitro System. It offers 4 dedicated physical cores at 2.8 GHz, 16.0 GB of memory, and 237 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage, backed by a 2 Gbps baseline network interface. Synthetic and application benchmarks show steady mid-range compute and memory performance, marked by 9.34 million Redis SET operations per second and strong single-threaded bzip3 decompression at 14.26 GB/sec. However, cryptographic PassMark operations and LLM text generation speeds benchmark in lower percentiles. The inclusion of fast local NVMe storage combined with a standard 1:4 CPU-to-memory profile makes the m8gd.xlarge cost-efficient for caching services, transactional databases, and containerized web workloads.
